specification.title: Kassir
specification.description: A Tauri v2 desktop cashier application (Point of Sale) for Windows. Sells and restocks goods, records arbitrary transactions, and keeps products, stock, customers, suppliers, payment methods, contacts, pockets and analytics. Offline-first: one SQLite database (data.db) is the source of truth, fronted by an Effect services layer (src/services/) whose SubscriptionRefs components subscribe to, and read through the page-data layer (src/components/page-data/). Includes thermal receipt printing (the layout and the PDF are built in Rust with printpdf, then handed to the Windows spooler), role-based access (admin/user), multi-cashier login, and a seq-based cloud sync of all eight groups (money, customer, supplier, method, social, extra, product, record) implemented as a background task (pull → merge → push → pull, manual trigger, status pill) whose contract is SYNC-V2.md — see <sync_system> and <sync_ui_design>.

conventions.rule: A page never touches SQLite, plugin-store or localStorage. Every read and write goes through a service (src/services/<name>). A service writes the database first, then its SubscriptionRef, so subscribers see the write with no refresh call. Bounded catalogs are a full-list ref (products, methods, extras, customers, suppliers, socials, cashiers, pockets); unbounded ones (records, money entries) are queried Effects plus a `revision` counter that a query puts in its deps.

Async page data goes through createPageData (src/components/page-data/): one key per independent read, the read lives at the leaf that renders the value, fine-grained gates with value-sized placeholders (never a whole-card swap), reserved card heights, a 200 ms anti-flash window, and writes that name the keys they invalidate. See <frontend> / page_data and .pi/skills/page-data.md.

Money arithmetic is decimal.js everywhere — never float `+ - *` on rupiah. `src/lib/purchase` holds the cart math (line subtotal/grand total, discount stack, extras, paid total, transaction grand total, roundMoney); the record's own precision (`record_fix`) is applied by `~/services/record/round.ts` (roundToFix) and by `roundMoney`, so the table and the printed receipt cannot disagree by a rounding step.

Dates are Temporal (temporal-polyfill) in the shop's time zone (`tz` in lib/constants), never the browser's raw Date arithmetic. A record belongs to the day `COALESCE(record_paid_at, record_credit_at, record_created_at)` says — the same effective date the day list, Beranda and Analytics use.

Bitfields are documented in FLAGS.md and defined beside their service: records.record_flag (RECORD_FLAG_ADJUSTMENT = 1), tx_records.tx_record_flag (STORED_FLAG = 0b01, ADJUSTMENT_CART_FLAG = 0b10), products.product_flag (PRODUCT_FLAG_UNPUBLISHED = 0b1), and the extras flags (DUAL_FLAG = 0b1, carried from extras into tx_extras into record_extras). Never reuse a bit.

Anything listening on `window` consults isScreenOwnedByDialog() (src/hooks/use-dialog-lock) before acting: a cart money editor is a `modal={false}` Radix dialog portaled beside #root, so `inert` and the focus trap do not stop a window keydown. useInertApp(open) registers the lock and makes #root inert/aria-hidden while the editor is open.
A page must not import another page's hook or helper. Shared behaviour is lifted to src/hooks or src/components, and shared page data to a service.

Services fail with a Data.TaggedError per domain (ProductError, RecordError, …). Pages either catch the typed failure (createErrorBoundary / pageData.Gate error prop) or render the sentence; the driver's text never reaches the screen (DbError splits `message` from `detail`).

command.name: hash_password
command.description: bcrypt at DEFAULT_COST on the blocking pool (~250 ms of CPU; running it inline would stall the command runtime). Returns the hash.

command.name: verify_password
command.signature: async fn(password: String, hash: String) → Result<bool, AuthError>
command.description: Verifies a plaintext password against a stored bcrypt hash, also on the blocking pool.

command.name: get_printers
command.description: Enumerates Windows printers via winprint. The error lists the available printers when a lookup fails.

command.name: print_receipt
command.signature: async fn(printer_name: String, data: ReceiptData, option: ReceiptOption) → Result<String, String>
command.description: Lays out the receipt and renders its one-page PDF in Rust (src-tauri/src/receipt/), validates the %PDF header, then prints it through the platform spooler path and returns the cashier-facing "Dikirim ke printer …" sentence. The PDF never crosses the IPC boundary in either direction, so this replaces the old generic print_pdf command (which the webview no longer had a reason to call). Runs on the blocking pool; the error is the cashier-facing "Gagal menyiapkan struk." or spooler sentence.

command.name: export_file
command.signature: async fn(default_name: String, contents: String) → Result<Option<String>, String>
command.description: The JSON download. The Save dialog and the write both live in Rust: the fs plugin's scope is narrowed to the app's own image and log directories, so a frontend writeFile on a user-picked path is rejected. Returns the written path, or None when the dialog was cancelled.

command.name: backup_data
command.signature: async fn(on_progress: Channel<BackupProgress>, store_json: String) → Result<Option<BackupSaved>, String>
command.description: The whole-install backup: Save dialog, then one `.zip` holding `data.db`, `store.json` and `manifest.json`. The database is snapshotted with `VACUUM INTO` through the live pool (not `fs::copy`) because `data.db` runs in WAL mode and a plain copy would silently omit every commit since the last checkpoint. The snapshot is `PRAGMA integrity_check`ed and switched to rollback-journal mode before it is shipped, the manifest records app version, `_sqlx_migrations` version, file digests and the destination directory of each file, and the archive is built beside the target and renamed into place so a failure never leaves a truncated `.zip` under the chosen name. `store_json` arrives from the frontend because the store plugin writes on a debounce and only the loaded instance knows the latest preference. Returns the path and byte size, or None when the dialog was cancelled. Progress comes back on a Channel as one monotonic bar for the whole run (snapshot → verify → hash → compress → finalize): the snapshot's slice is estimated from the growing temp file against `page_count × page_size`, because `VACUUM INTO` reports nothing while it runs, and the hash and compress slices count the bytes they read. Stage timings are logged.

command.name: sync_pull
command.signature: async fn(channel, base_url, token, group, after, limit, client) → Result<StreamSummary, SyncFailure>
command.description: GET /v2/<group>/pull/:seq?limit=N: reads the response body chunk by chunk, cuts it into NDJSON lines at the newlines (holding a split line until it completes), and pushes one line per Channel message followed by an explicit end message. `group` is validated against the eight known groups before it becomes a path segment. Advertises Accept-Encoding: gzip and lets reqwest decode it, so the lines are always canonical plaintext. A non-2xx body's `floor` (on a 410) is carried through to the frontend. This is the polyfill for the Streams API the contract is written against; the webview cannot fetch the sync host at all under its CSP, nor read a streamed body under ipc:.

command.name: sync_push
command.signature: async fn(channel, base_url, token, group, body, client) → Result<StreamSummary, SyncFailure>
command.description: POST /v2/<group>/push: sends one NDJSON batch (bare `{"e":…,"r":{…}}` row lines, or one `{"e":"record","r":{…},"ch":{…}}` aggregate per record, within the group's frame/byte bound) and streams the ack lines back over the channel. Stateless: no session, no offset, no content coding to negotiate.

command.name: sync_health
command.signature: async fn(base_url, token, client) → Result<HealthReport, SyncFailure>
command.description: GET /v2/health: the Cek button's one request — does this token work against this server right now? Sends the same Authorization and X-Kassir-* identity headers as pull/push, with a 15 s timeout (a health check is a button someone is watching, not a sync). A 2xx returns the status plus the body collapsed to one bounded line; anything else is a SyncFailure, so the screen shows the server's own sentence inline.

command.name: sync_merge
command.signature: async fn(app, plan: { statements: [{ sql, bindings }] }) → Result<{ statements }, MergeFailure>
command.description: Applies a whole pull in ONE transaction. plugin-sql's surface cannot: it keeps its `execute` statement-by-statement in autocommit and exposes no transaction handle. This command borrows the plugin's own pool instead of opening a second connection — the plugin publishes `DbInstances(pub RwLock<HashMap<String, DbPool>>)` and `DbPool::Sqlite(Pool<Sqlite>)` for exactly this — so there is one set of connections, one configuration and no lock-contention window in which the POS's own writes could fail. Statements are generated in TS (`services/sync/sql.ts`); Rust only binds and executes, so the column order the wire contract freezes is the same one the SQL uses. One call = one transaction: a pull page, or one push batch's acks, land whole or not at all. The bookmark is written after the commit, so a failure re-pulls the same page (idempotent, §6.5).

command.name: sync_cancel
command.description: Flips the cancellation flag the streaming commands registered under request_id; the read loop checks it between chunks, so a cancelled sync stops the HTTP request instead of draining it in the background. Reached by an explicit cancel (the status pill's dialog or the Sinkronisasi panel) — leaving a screen no longer cancels anything, because the run is a background task.

command.name: sync_blob_manifest
command.signature: async fn(base_url, token, after: Option<String>, limit, client) → Result<BlobManifest, SyncFailure>
command.description: GET /v2/product/image/manifest: one JSON page of {image_id, version, sha256, byte_size, mime}, paged by image_id. A join over the entity tables, not a log — no seq, no ETag, no bookmark. The body is parsed with serde_json rather than reqwest's json feature, which this build does not enable.

command.name: sync_blob_put
command.signature: async fn(base_url, token, image_id, version, file_name, mime, client) → Result<BlobPut, SyncFailure>
command.description: PUT /v2/product/image/blob/:image_id?version=: reads AppData/images/<file_name> (the row's image_name; rejected if it could leave the folder), refuses over 8 MB before sending, and posts the bytes as a raw body with the row's mime. The row must already exist on the server, which is why the client pushes rows first. A missing local file answers the code `local_missing` (status 0) — not a server error: the caller forgets the version it recorded and fetches the picture instead. Returns the digest the server stored, the `deduped` and the `current` flags.

command.name: sync_blob_get
command.signature: async fn(base_url, token, sha256, file_name, client) → Result<BlobGet, SyncFailure>
command.description: GET /v2/blob/:sha256: streams the object into images/<file_name>.part, hashing chunk by chunk and refusing past 8 MB, then verifies the byte count and the digest and only then rename()s it onto images/<file_name> (same directory, so the replace is atomic). Anything that does not match removes the scratch file and leaves the previous picture untouched. Accept-Encoding is identity: the body is verified against the published digest, and a transparent decode would make Content-Length describe the wrong bytes.

security.description: No embedded HTTP server and no JWT. Passwords hash and verify through the two bcrypt commands above; the session is frontend state (the auth service), persisted in localStorage. The sync credential is the single-tenant SYNC_TOKEN (§10 of the sync contract), typed by the operator and kept in store.json (sync.token) — never compiled into the binary; the server address is an operator setting too (sync.base_url, seeded with SYNC_DEFAULT_BASE_URL = https://api.kassir.store), so one build can talk to a self-hosted backend. All sync HTTP goes through the Rust client: it keeps the window CSP at connect-src 'self' ipc: instead of allowing every origin, and it is the only way to consume the NDJSON streams.
security.single_instance: tauri-plugin-single-instance is registered first, before any window or database work. The model is one process per machine: data.db is preloaded and the catalogue/cart live in process-local refs, so a second launch would debounce-write its own stale snapshot over the first. A second launch focuses the existing window instead.

database.name: data.db
database.description:
The only database. Every migration in src-tauri/src/database/<range>/migration-N.sql is embedded by database/mod.rs and applied on boot; the frontend also applies the same files in the e2e harness. The schema evolved from INTEGER keys to TEXT (ULID) keys with `_updated_at` / `_sync_at` bookkeeping. Key steps: - 1-10: initial tables (products, records, record_items), discounts, rounding, credit, capital - 11-20: barcode to TEXT, capital fixes, cashiers with a password hash, record redesign - 21-30: price/capital to REAL, images, socials, money, payment methods - 31-40: TEXT (ULID) keys, product_events (event-sourced stock), sync columns; money-kind renamed to pocket - 41: pocket ordering (money_kind_ordering, carried onto pockets later) - 42: extras.extra_flag - 43: the schema rewrite — products split into listings / properties / images / stocks, records into record_listings / record_methods / record_extras / record_images / discounts, every syncable row gains a `<singular>_deleted_at` soft-delete column (graves/graves_kind retired), and the tx_* cart tables are ported into data.db (tx.db is no longer preloaded). Replaced tables are parked as `<name>_old`; nothing was dropped - 44: the backfill — every old row copied into the new shape, parent-first, no DDL - 45: a no-op bridge slot, so databases that recorded a 46 from another branch still line up - 46: adds image/webp to img_mimes - 47: queues every syncable row for its first upload (all `_sync_at` markers cleared), since the sync server was created from zero for the byte-stream protocol and has never seen this device's rows; enables the forcing migration-44 step 13 had left commented out - 48: drops the parked `<name>_old` tables - 49: the sync client contract — opaque cross-device references, `record_flag`, `record_pair_id` - 50: `image_blob_*` columns (the image-byte side channel) - 51: the stock-fold index (product_events by stock) - 52: the record-dirty partial index on `records (record_updated_at, record_id)` - 53: categories and the product_category join, carried in the product sync group - 54: repairs `record_listing_capital` — see below - 55: makes the category tables mergeable: no key from a link to its category and no unique name or pair index, because a pull page may carry a link before its category (or a name/pair a second till created) and must store it rather than fail the commit. The one-live-row rules move to `CategoryService` - 56: the same treatment for the three product children `migration-43` keyed: one live barcode, one live property key and one live alias are rules of `ProductService`, not indexes, so a second till's row is stored instead of failing the page - 57: combo templates with ordered listing/quantity and Extra-preset children plus an optional cover reference; the sync marker is reserved, but combos are not registered in a sync group Read indexes for the hot queries (records' effective date, listings, product_events' product/stock/record) are created in 43.
Migration 54 is the one data-repair step, and the reason `get.margins` has an estimate at all. The v1 app wrote the *selling price* into `record_product_capital_raw` from ~2026-01, and migration-44 copied that column into `record_listings.record_listing_capital` and the journal it rebuilt — so 98% of 2026 revenue carried a cost equal to its price and every margin read zero or negative. The old tables are gone (48), so 54 reconstructs each polluted sale's cost from the last purchase of the same product at or before it, fixes the matching `product_events.product_event_capital`, and re-folds `stocks.stock_capital` from the journal with the sync projection's rule (newest non-zero event). Idempotent; lines with no cost at all and products never purchased are left for the Profit page's estimate.

routing.description: Hash router (createHashRouter) in src/route.tsx. Pages are imported eagerly except three deliberate lazy boundaries: the Home page body (the heaviest dashboard), Analytics' five bodies (recharts + d3), and the product Performance tab. The receipt adds no bundle: its layout and PDF are rendered by the Rust print_receipt command. The Dev/PageData and Dev/PageCache playgrounds only exist when `import.meta.env.DEV` is true.

guards.description: There is no route middleware. Protection is the AuthLayout component plus in-page role checks, and the shortcuts are not role-gated, so the in-page check is what actually stops a non-admin.
guards.guard: Subscribes to service.auth.changes; while the session resolves it renders a loader, on null it redirects to /login. Wraps every route but /login.
Children for admins, `<Redirect to={fallback}>` for everyone else. Used by Setting shop/data/log, Extra new and Combo management.
Renders `<Redirect to="/">` itself when useUser().role is not admin.
Admins get the edit form; other roles get a read-only info panel.
guards.note: Setting printer is reachable by any signed-in user: the sidebar hides it from non-admins but the route is ungated (see <open_questions>).

layouts.layout: The session guard, the sticky Topbar, the main-body scrollport, the Outlet, the sonner Toaster, the alt+N shortcuts and the close-flush handler. The shell is h-dvh with #main-body as `flex-1 min-h-0 overflow-y-auto`: pages get a definite height from this chain, which is what every `h-full` page and its scroll box relies on — do not go back to min-height on the shell. Back button (unless on "/"), the route title (longest-prefix map), the dynamic shop title, TopNavList, Refresh and SettingLink. Desktop tab bar: Toko (/pos), Restock (/restock), Produk (/products), Riwayat (/records), Uang (/money, admin only). The shop name from the info service, shown once the form has answered. window.location.reload(); there is no cache to bust. Gear → /setting, with the alt+5 hint. alt+0..5 navigation, alt legend toggle, dialog-lock and editable-target guards. On window close, flushes the cart service and destroys the window; `core:window:allow-destroy` exists for it. @xstate/store atom for the 5-second Kbd legend.

auth_module.description: src/lib/auth.ts is only the two Tauri bridges — hash(password) and verify(password, storedHash) — plus the Unauthenticated error. The session lives in the auth service: persisted under the localStorage key "user" through the hidden local-storage service, validated with a Zod schema { id, name, role }, and checked against the cashiers table on hydrate (a session pointing at a deleted cashier is dropped and the key cleared). auth.get / auth.set / auth.changes drive the guard, useUser() and the topbar.

page_data.description: src/components/page-data/ — the async-data convention every page follows. createPageData<Data, Error>(name, { cache }) returns a typed namespace: `Provider` registers the page's sources (a Stream per key, keyed by name) and starts them together; `Gate` renders a set of keys with a pulse placeholder, an error slot, a delay (200 ms anti-flash by default) and a render prop that receives exactly the gated values; `use(key)` reads one key without gating; `useFrame(keys)` returns the status and first error for a static frame that must survive a failure; `useStatus` / `useRefresh` / `useMutate` cover the rest. The cache (z-cache.ts, exported as `pageCache`) keeps the last answer per tag+deps in memory, paints it on a return visit, and invalidates on a write or a revision bump; `Dev/PageCache` is its inspector.
page_data.component: keys, pulse, error (node or typed render prop), delay, children({...values}). The old Result-based Gate survives only in Dev/PageData, which demonstrates the difference.
Holds the region's space from the first frame but stays invisible for the anti-flash window (useDelayedFlag). For regions whose shape the skeleton authors (forms, a total's box).
The real control, disabled and empty, with only its text pulsing — the box, border, padding and chevron never move.

page_data.rule: Two reads that fail independently get two keys. A value that needs two reads declares both; a value that needs one declares one, so it can land first.
A card's floor is a min-height (ROWS_FLOOR), never a measurement, so the skeleton and the real content occupy the same box.
A page does not block on one top-level Loader: chrome is on the first frame, values fill in (or pulse) inside it.

cart.description: The POS machinery in src/components/cart/, shared by Pos (sale), Restock (purchase) and, for its tab model, /transaction. A cart is a `tx_records` row plus tx_listings / tx_discounts / tx_extras / tx_methods / tx_images, owned by the transaction service; every edit is written through, so a refresh reopens the same cart. The open cart and the stage are URL values (`?draft=`, `?stage=`), and tab switches replace history.
cart.component: The draft lifecycle: always have a cart, start one on demand, open/close/store/restore tabs, the tab walker (Ctrl+Arrow), F1/F2/F12, the dialog lock, and the stage reset on tab switch.

The goods grid — one line per row, editable cells (name/code/unit/price/qty/discount), per-cell issues, the search panel, scan-to-add, clipboard, undo.
The payment strip: one row per method of a kind, split payments, Ctrl+0..3 kind swap, the money editors as `modal={false}` dialogs with useInertApp.
The charge grid: preset catalog search, percent/number kinds, the dual-flag charge carried into the record.
The keyboard model: columns, rows, selection, editing, and the per-column constraints, kept pure so the grids cannot drift apart.
Kind vs method: a kind offers its named accounts then its base method; freeMethodId/nextFreeKind/kindExhausted enforce one method per transaction.
The duplicate/unregistered-code checks that block Bayar, with links to the products involved.
The completion dialog's tender rows: zero rows dropped, base methods labelled from their kind, a deleted method keeps its money.
CartBody (the completion dialog's stable slot) and CartPanels (the `inert` panel column with the blocking overlay while submitting).

Role guard / hash-router-aware redirect (optional hard reload).
Conditional render (by `when`, or by `value` where only null/undefined fall through) and the keyed array map.

The locale-aware numeric input (caret survives grouping dots), the password field with reveal, the import file panel (keyboard-reachable, drop or click), and the payment-method picker (kind + account).

The date picker, the URL-driven range picker, and the Temporal-backed date+time field (a DateTimeField, never a native datetime-local). DateTime's optional `max` is a wall, not a fence: a reading past it stays pickable, and the complaint (`Tidak bisa memilih waktu di masa depan setelah <YYYY mmmm DD, HH.MM>`) waits for `showError` — set after a refused Simpan, or by the picker's own `onBlur` where the control has no submit. testing.description: Three layers, plus mechanical guards. Unit tests sit beside the code as *.test.ts(x) and are run by `bun test` (happy-dom preloaded, @testing-library matchers, afterEach cleanup). Integration tests live in src/integration/ and wire the real service layers over the real migrations with only the Tauri backends substituted (db/store/local-storage test-support). End-to-end specs live in e2e/ and drive /e2e.html, whose in-browser harness (src/e2e/) runs the same migration files on sql.js and injects the service before the router is imported.
testing.layer: *.test.ts(x) beside the module; service tests use makeTestDatabase (bun:sqlite + every migration) and the Map-backed store/local-storage fakes; page/data hook tests use a real MemoryRouter; Tauri commands are stubbed with mock.module at the module boundary.

src/integration/: the real service layers over the real migrations, the real page-data layer and the real page components — only the Tauri backends are substituted. home.test.tsx (Beranda's keys over the record/money services), product-page.test.tsx (catalogue reads and write-through), shop-settings.test.tsx (Setting → Toko's form writing to the store), and the till pair pos.test.tsx + restock.test.tsx. The till pair drives the cart screens the way the operator does: scan into the grid (type + Enter before the debounce), bump a quantity, edit the inline tender, walk Restock's stages, open the completion dialog, park a tab, press F12 / Ctrl+Arrow / F2. What it pins is the joins — a scan becomes a line and a total, Bayar gates on the tender, a commit writes the record and moves stock the right way, a credit purchase books a debt, a dual charge commits its extras-only twin, Batalkan rewinds a sale into a draft. `till-harness.tsx` builds a fresh database, store, session and service per test and offers the common helpers; `service-proxy.ts` is the injection seam.
testing.rule: Integration tests hand the pages a service through `src/integration/service-proxy.ts` (a stable proxy over `globalThis.__KASSIR_SERVICE__`, set per test) instead of `mock.module("~/services")`: bun caches a module across test files, so a second file's mock never takes effect and the pages keep the first file's service.
testing.layer: e2e/*.e2e.ts via Playwright against /e2e.html: seeded SQL/storage, a real login, then assertions on the actual screens (pos-cart, transaction, analytics, publish, page-data, page-cache, …).

guards.guard: No raw text sizes, no lucide size={N}; the four text tokens are the hierarchy.
Every DialogContent has a DialogDescription or an explicit aria-describedby={undefined}.
The shipped capability stays least-privilege (no fs:default, no updater, no process).
The version constant matches package.json (a release that forgets one bump site fails).

connection.description: One database, data.db, preloaded by @tauri-apps/plugin-sql and migrated on boot by the embedded Rust migration list. The only frontend accessor is the hidden `db` service (src/services/db/) — domain services never touch plugin-sql themselves. DatabaseService exposes execute, selectMany, selectOne and transaction, each wrapped in Effect with a DbError. `transaction` joins its statements into one execute call: plugin-sql has no transaction handle, but a single execute is atomic, so a cross-table write is one multi-statement string with renumbered placeholders. Raw SQL, parameterized; no ORM. The handle is opened in WAL mode on first load (`journal.ts`, best effort, one `PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL`): the mode is a property of the file and sqlx deliberately leaves it alone, so without it a fresh install ran in rollback-journal mode — writers were blocking the constant reads behind them, and a background merge would have made that visible mid-sale. A filesystem that refuses `-wal` (a network share) keeps its mode; the app still opens.
connection.file: DatabaseService interface, Binding/Statement types, DbError { message, detail }.
DatabaseLive — a lazily loaded handle behind Layer.succeed, opened through journal.ts.
enableWriteAheadLog — the one PRAGMA, best effort, logged, never fatal.

Tables replaced by 43 are parked as `<name>_old` and are never read; nothing was dropped, so they remain on disk.

caching.description: A service's SubscriptionRef is the cache: reads come from the ref once hydrated; a write goes to SQLite first and then updates the ref, so subscribers see it with no explicit refresh. Queried domains (records, money entries, analytics) expose a `revision` counter instead, which a query puts in its deps. The one sanctioned revalidate is product.refresh()/refreshMany(), because a record or transaction write moves stock behind the product aggregate's back. On top of that, page-data's pageCache keeps the last answer per tag+deps in memory and invalidates on writes/revisions; it never touches disk.

cart_tables.description: The tab-based cart, ported into data.db by migration 43 (tx.db is no longer preloaded). Not synced. A tab is a `tx_records` row; its goods are `tx_listings`, its charges `tx_extras`, its payments `tx_methods`, its line discounts `tx_discounts` (hanging off a listing), its pictures `tx_images`. Committing writes the record and deletes the tab in one transaction; `transaction.add.fromRecord` rebuilds a tab from a saved record, and `record.delete` on a record it came from never leaves a stale tab behind.

record_commit.description: Three writers, all in the record service, all one multi-statement transaction: `record.add.draft` (a live cart: header, lines, discounts, extras, payments, stock movement, tx_* delete), `record.add.external` (an imported record, under a new id) and `record.add.adjustment` (a hand-typed extras-only record, flagged RECORD_FLAG_ADJUSTMENT). A sale drains `stocks` oldest-first (a purchase receives a new cost lot) through the pure builders in product/stock-sql.ts. A purchase's capital: its per-pc cost is the grand total split by each line's own total, then rounded to the record's `record_fix` before it reaches `stocks.stock_capital` and `record_listings.record_listing_capital` — the same precision lot matching and the Modal column compare with. When a draft's DUAL_FLAG extras are present, `add.draft` also writes the extras-only `outcoming` twin in the same commit, both rows stamped with each other's id in `record_pair_id`. A line that points at a catalogue listing is also the operator's latest word on the goods (record/sql/catalogue.ts): its edited name is written back to listings.listing_name — and to products.product_name when that product has a single live listing — while its price is written back only on a sale and only in the listing's own unit. Codes and units are never written back; the record keeps its own snapshot either way.

services.description: Domain state lives in Effect services at src/services/<name>/ — index.ts is the interface only, live.ts is the Layer. Each owns a SubscriptionRef as its single source of truth and exposes reads as Effects plus a changes Stream; a write goes to SQLite first and then the ref. Components subscribe with useStream/useQuery or, preferably, through page-data. Typed errors are caught by createErrorBoundary or rendered per key by pageData.Gate. src/services/index.ts composes the layers and exports the app-level `service` object. Public services: analytics, auth, cashier, category, combo, config, customer, extra, info, listing, log, method, money, printer, product, record, social, supplier, sync, transaction, zoom. Hidden backends: db, store, local-storage. Sync additionally injects its transport (SyncTransportService) so the loops can be tested against an in-memory server.

hidden_backends.backend: execute / selectMany / selectOne / transaction over data.db; DbError { message, detail }. See <database>.

Sales per local hour, and per ISO weekday (1 = Monday).

Every product that moved, with qty, revenue, margin, costed lines. `margin` uses the same believable-cost rule as `get.margins` — a stored cost above zero and below the line's price — so the two pages never disagree about whether a line's cost can be read as one; the rest of the lines count towards `lines` only.

Applying a level also writes `--icon-scale` (1/√zoom, `iconScaleOf`) to the document root: global.css multiplies every lucide stroke by it, so a 200% interface grows its glyphs without turning hairline outlines into marker pens. service.name: product
service.description: The product aggregate: a product with its listings (priced units, at most one code each, unique across live listings), properties, alternative names, images and stock lots. The read model's `stock` and `capital` are derived — the sum of the lots and their weighted-average cost. Owns products, listings, properties, product_names, images, stocks, product_events and the `product_category` links; the category names are `CategoryService`'s. `ProductFull.categoryIds` carries the live link ids, which the form draws as one badge each, and a name typed into its picker is a *draft* name (`ProductDraft.newCategories`) rather than a row: the save creates it and files the product under the id that comes back, so a name typed and never saved costs the catalogue nothing. `ProductInput.categoryIds` files a new product in the same transaction that creates it. The child keys a shop thinks of as unique — one live barcode, one live property key per product, one live alias per product — are this service's rules (`listing.add/update`, `product.add`, `property.add/update`, `productName.add/update`), not indexes on the tables: migration 56 dropped them so a second till's row is stored by the sync instead of failing the page.
service.error: Plus ProductDuplicateCode, carrying the code that was already taken.
service.state: One SubscriptionRef of the whole read model; a write re-hydrates the touched rows, and get.changes / changesFull / unsync read from it.

An in-memory lookup over the same ref `get.byId` reads.
One transaction: the product, at least one listing, optional codes, one stock lot and the category links. Values are validated here (no negative price or cost basis from any writer).

Make the live links exactly this list: insert the new ones, tombstone the dropped ones, one transaction. A list that changes nothing writes nothing (no clock bump, so nothing re-enters the push queue).

service.name: record
service.description: Committed transactions and everything snapshotted with them: listing lines with their discounts, extras, split payments and images. Owns records, record_listings, record_methods, record_extras, record_images and discounts. The mode follows the money, not the goods: `incoming` is a sale (money in, stock consumed), `outcoming` a purchase (money out, stock received).
service.state: Records are a queried domain (always read by range), so there is no full-list ref: reads are Effects and get.revision is a counter bumped on every write, which a queried page puts in its deps.

Capped page of matching lines plus the total match count; a blank query returns nothing.
Unsettled credit records, newest first.
Write counter a queried page re-reads on.
Per-mode count and sum for a range.
A hand-typed extras-only record (RECORD_FLAG_ADJUSTMENT); no stock moves.
Import a record made elsewhere under a new id, moving stock by the same rules as a live record.

Commit a live cart: header, lines, discounts, extras, payments, stock movement and the tx_* delete, in one transaction; with `mirror`, the DUAL_FLAG twin is written in the same commit. See <database> / record_commit.

method.name: set.paidAt / set.creditAt / set.note / set.mode / set.payment / set.toCredit / set.payCredit / set.lineCapital

interface.note: set.lineCapital is the escape hatch for a `modal` entered with the wrong figure: a sale carries a copy of its lot's cost, so one bad purchase line makes every later sale of that product read as a huge loss. It rewrites `record_listings.record_listing_capital` for every portion of the line (the figure is a cost per listing unit), bumps record_updated_at, clears record_sync_at, and appends `Perbaikan modal <name>: <old> → <new> — <reason> (<admin>)` to record_note. It never touches product_events or stocks: the lot is a separate repair with a wider blast radius. Refuses a blank reason, a negative/non-finite figure, and a line outside the record; restating the same figure writes nothing. Admin-only in the UI (the pencil beside the Modal column on the record page's ledger).

set.mode does not rewrite the record in place: it soft-deletes the original, re-points every child at a copy and flips the stock journal, returning the new id — the page follows it instead of sitting on a tombstone.

set.payment rewrites every record_methods row from the submitted list (re-file a method, restate an amount, add or trim a split) and re-caches record_pay; the totals never move. The sum must cover the grand total (an underpayment is a credit), and an outstanding credit refuses it — its money arrives with set.payCredit. set.mode flips sale ↔ purchase and revisits the stock rules, striking the old movement from the journal first.
interface.method: Soft-delete and reverse the stock movement. A paired record takes its twin with it, so voiding a sale never leaves the extras-only outcoming half behind.

service.name: sync
service.description: The device's mirror of all eight groups (see <sync_system>). Owns the pull → merge → push → pull cycle as a background task (a daemon fiber in the service, one run at a time, overlapping triggers coalesced into one more pass), the SQLite bookmark and park, and the mirror SQL. Files: schema.ts (every group's column dictionaries and limits), frames.ts (NDJSON encode/decode, rows and the record aggregate), sql.ts (guarded upserts, markers, aggregate replacement, unsync reads, bookmark/park/reset statements), merge.ts (the four merge kinds, the page apply, the missing-pocket park), pull.ts / push.ts / retry.ts (the two loops and the shared backoff), stream.ts (the Channel→stream polyfill), transport.ts (the Rust commands as a service), blob.ts (the image-byte side channel: the upload pass and the manifest+download pass), live.ts (wiring, per-group cycle, single-flight start, coalesced progress, re-seed, refresh).
service.error: message plus the contract's optional code/status/floor, so the loops can branch on bad_request / too_old / bad_frame / payload_too_large.

interface.method: The server address and bearer token, from store.json (sync.base_url / sync.token); the address is seeded with SYNC_DEFAULT_BASE_URL when unset.

Pings GET /v2/health at the address currently in the Settings field with the token currently in it (not the stored pair), returning the server's status and one-line message — what the Cek button asks before anything is saved.
This installation's id, minted on first read and persisted in store.json (sync.device_id), sent as X-Kassir-Device-Id and shown in Settings.
The money group's bookmark: the highest `seq` durably stored, one integer for both tables.

The cycle itself, owned by the caller's fiber: mode "sync" | "reset" (reset first clears the bookmark, drops the park and marks every pocket and money row unsynced), returning { lastPulledSeq, pulled, pushed, stale }. Used by `start` and by the tests; the app never calls it directly.

Forks the loop as a daemon and returns "started" | "already-running". Single-flight: a second call while a run is in flight is refused, never started alongside it. Resolves as soon as the fiber exists — the outcome arrives through `state`.

Stream<SyncState>: status (idle | preparing | pull | merge | push | cancelling | done | failed | cancelled), entity, done/total, message, startedAt/finishedAt, report, error. Replays the current value to every subscriber, so the pill can mount mid-run. Progress is coalesced to ~150 ms; every transition is published immediately.
Asks the running loop to stop. Cooperative: the interrupt lands at the next async boundary (a page commit or a batch), so the activity reads `cancelling` until it does, then `cancelled`.

service.note: No domain service exposes the raw unsync rows (a soft-deleted row is not in any ref), so the sync service runs the mirror SQL itself and then calls the owning service's refresh() — MoneyService owns both pockets and money. This is the one place the rule "all reads/writes go through the owning service (or a new sync service)" needs the parenthetical.

service.name: transaction
service.description: The open carts in tx_* tables, and the one place a cart becomes history. Owns tx_records, tx_listings, tx_discounts, tx_extras, tx_methods and tx_images. Every edit is written through (debounced), so a refresh reopens the same cart; a failed write surfaces through get.saveError rather than disappearing. Commit goes through record.add.draft; the adjustment screen commits through record.add.adjustment.
service.error: Plus SubmitError, a refusal the cashier can act on, whose `kind` lets the page route it (empty | stored | payment | name | code | price | outcoming).

interface.method: The open carts, oldest order first.
Stream<string | null>: null while every edit is on disk, a sentence once a write failed.
Write pending edits now; put a failure on the same channel.

cloud_api.description: The wire contract is SYNC-V2-MONEY.md (protocol 2, group `money`), not the retired backend-docs/sync-contract.md or backend-docs/openapi.yaml. Both directions are newline-delimited JSON and both are stateless — no session, no offset, no hash chain: a pull is `GET /v2/money/pull/:seq?limit=`, a push is `POST /v2/money/push` with a bare row-frame NDJSON body, both behind `Authorization: Bearer kst_…`. The server numbers every applied change (`seq`), keeps the history, and the client stores one integer — its bookmark. The HTTP client lives in Rust (src-tauri/src/sync.rs) — see <rust> <commands> — because the window CSP (connect-src 'self' ipc:) forbids the sync host and the webview cannot read a streamed body under ipc:.

sync_system.description: Sync v2, grouped by tables. All eight groups ship: `money` (pockets + ledger), `customer`, `supplier`, `method`, `social`, `extra`, `product` (catalog, categories and stock journal) and `record` (the sale aggregate). Contract: SYNC-V2.md. A group is an independent stream: its own endpoint pair, its own column dictionaries, its own bookmark. The service runs pull → merge → push → pull per group, in `SYNC_GROUPS` order, and reports one `GroupState` per group so the UI shows a progress bar each. `cashiers`, `cashier_roles`, `stocks` (derived from the event journal), the `tx_*` cart tables and enum tables are local-only; image **rows** sync in the `product` group, and image **bytes** travel over that group's content-addressed side channel (§8.7.1) — no seq, no log entry, no bookmark.
sync_system.note: Combo templates are not one of the eight implemented groups and must not be mistaken for synced catalog data. A future parent aggregate, cross-group reference, deletion and image-byte design is documented in docs/docs/architecture/combos.md; no combo sync code ships yet.

schema_contract.item: schema.ts freezes every entity's column order once (the 16 row entities, of which one is the record aggregate, plus its five child sets); the encoder (frames.ts), the merge statements (sql.ts) and the reset path all resolve through it. Every column is always present, `null` is explicit, timestamps are epoch-ms integers. Key order is not load-bearing: v2 has no hashing.

`sync_bookmark(group_name, seq)` in SQLite — one integer per group, advanced to `done.s` (not `meta.snapshot`: a page can stop early) and written in the SAME transaction as the page's rows. A pre-table database reads its `sync.<group>.bookmark` store key once and migrates it.

`sync_parked_money(money_id, seq, row_json)` holds money rows whose pocket is not on the device yet. They are never dropped and never abort a page; every later page retries them, keyed by id so a re-pulled page parks one row once. Written with the page's bookmark.

`<x>_sync_at` is the push marker and holds the server's `seq`: NULL means owed. Merged rows are marked immediately so they are not pushed back. Every marker and `stale` write is guarded on the row's clock, so an edit that lands while its frame is in flight is not lost (§4.12).

Every local edit writes `<x>_updated_at = max(now, <x>_updated_at + 1)` (SQL scalar max) and clears the dirty flag in the same statement, so two edits in one millisecond cannot tie (§5.1.1). A soft delete sets both `_deleted_at` and `_updated_at` to that clock.

Dropped the cross-group foreign keys a pulled aggregate may dangle against (`records.record_supplier_id`, `records.record_pair_id`, `record_listings.product_id`/`product_event_id`, `record_methods.method_id`, `product_events.product_id`/`stock_id`/`record_id`), and added `sync_bookmark` + `sync_parked_money`. The local write paths that relied on those constraints (payment methods) now check explicitly.

Added the three client-only byte columns to `images` (`image_blob_version` / `image_blob_sha256` / `image_blob_sync_at`) and set every live row's version to its clock: in this product the bytes of one image_id never change and a file under images/ was written by whichever device created the row, so an existing file is the current version's bytes. A row whose file is missing is cleared again on its first upload attempt (`local_missing`) and fetched instead. A pull merge never touches the trio.

Made the category tables mergeable, because every constraint 53 added could be violated by a legal frame and a page that fails to commit is a group that never moves again. `product_category` lost its key to `categories` (the scoped product sync never carries categories, so a link can arrive before its category) and its unique `(product_id, category_id)` pair (the server keeps both rows when two tills tick the same box). `categories` lost its unique live name (two tills may create "Minuman" offline; `kassir-server` keeps no such key either). The one-live-row-per-name and one-live-link-per-pair rules stay, as checks in `CategoryService` and the product form, where a duplicate a user creates is refused but one that arrives through sync is kept.

The same rule for the last three keys `migration-43` put on a synced table: `listings (listing_code NOCASE)`, `properties (product_id, property_key)` and `product_names (product_id, product_name_value)`, one live row each. Two tills that were offline can assign the same barcode, add the same key or record the same alias, and the server keeps both; a unique index here made that legal page fail its commit and stranded the product group. The rules moved into `ProductService` (and `validateProductInput` for the two rows one import can carry), which is where the operator is told about them.

shape.stage: `GET /v2/<group>/pull/:seq?limit=<default>` per page, decoding `meta` / `row` / `ag` / `del` / `done` lines as they stream; an unknown `t` or another group's entity is skipped, never fatal. A transport/5xx failure is retried with exponential full jitter (base 1 s, cap 60 s). Nothing is written during the read, so the bookmark cannot run ahead of the data.

One page = one statement batch through the Rust `sync_merge` command, i.e. one real transaction on the plugin's own pool (plugin-sql exposes no transaction handle), with `PRAGMA defer_foreign_keys` so a child may precede its parent in the page. Row entities are processed in the group's dependency order (pockets before money; product before children before the journal); a money row whose pocket is unknown is parked. The bookmark, the park and the rows commit together.

The §5 rule per kind, applied in three places with the same result: plain LWW (pocket, customer, supplier, method, social, extra and the five catalog entities), the money ledger rule (insert / note edit / soft delete; `timestamp`, `money_value`, `pocket_id` immutable), append-only (`product_event`) and aggregate LWW (`record`: header + five child sets replaced wholesale). Each write repeats the comparison in SQL so a cashier's edit during the merge is not overwritten.

The rows/records whose `_sync_at IS NULL`, in the group's order, within the frame and byte bounds (1000 / 1 MB; record 1000 / 8 MB), `POST /v2/<group>/push`. One ack per frame: `applied` / `noop` set `_sync_at = seq`; `stale` carries the server's winning row/aggregate, which is force-written unless the local row changed after its frame left (then it stays unsynced and is re-pushed). A record is one frame; a record over 8 MB is surfaced, never skipped. A failed batch is re-sent whole, with backoff on transport/5xx.

After every page and again after the push, the owning service is re-read (money, customer, supplier, method, social, extra, product) or its revision bumped (record), so the running UI sees the merged rows.

The `product` group's second channel, outside every transaction above. **After a page commits**: read the manifest once (paged, two pages at most), then for each live image row whose `image_blob_version` is not its clock and whose manifest entry names exactly that clock, `GET /v2/blob/:sha256` into images/<image_name> (`.part` + verify + rename) and record the digest; an equal digest only moves the bookkeeping (a reorder elsewhere changes the clock, not the picture); a row with no manifest entry is a placeholder, never a download. **After the push**: upload the rows whose clock equals `image_blob_version`, whose bytes were never accepted and whose row the server already has (`image_sync_at IS NOT NULL`), 20 per pass. `local_missing` forgets the version (turning the row into a fetch), `blob_conflict` adopts the server's copy, `image_unknown`/`image_deleted` wait for the pull, and every other failure is logged and retried next cycle — bytes never fail the group and never gate the bookmark (§8.7.1).

Pull `400`/`410` → the bookmark came from somewhere else: bookmark `0` on a `400` and the server's `floor` on a `410`, every synced row marked dirty (content and clocks untouched), then pull → push. Nothing is deleted; the same procedure seeds a group with no backfill (§13.4). `401` stops every group; other group failures are reported and the run continues.

requirements.item: The sync service owns the mirror SQL; pages never reach it. It refreshes the owning service's ref after each page and each batch.

A tombstone (`_deleted_at`) is an ordinary row whose payload says "deleted at T" and merges like any update. Deleting a pocket soft-deletes its money rows; deleting a product sends child tombstones; deleting a record keeps its children. A live child under a soft-deleted parent is an orphan: kept, hidden and counted, never auto-deleted (§6.6).
A group is independent: own bookmark, own park, own progress entry, own entry in schema.ts. One cycle per group at a time; overlapping triggers coalesce into one more pass.
The contract is written against ReadableStream; the Tauri commands `sync_pull` / `sync_push` polyfill it over an IPC channel (src/services/sync/stream.ts).
`GET /v2/health` must answer `protocol: 2` before the first group route of a session; a plain-`http` base URL is refused unless it names the local machine.

sync_ui_design.description: Manual sync only (automatic sync is a v2 idea). Setting → Sinkronisasi (admin-only) is two numbered panels. "1. Server": the server address (an operator setting seeded with SYNC_DEFAULT_BASE_URL) and a SYNC_TOKEN field, both saved to store.json, plus the last pull cursor and a Cek button that pings /v2/health at that address with that token and renders the answer inline next to Simpan — so a typo is caught before it is written to disk. "2. Sinkronisasi": the action. Its buttons stay DISABLED until the address and token are stored — a sync with no credential can only fail, and the failure would be about the field the operator was already meant to fill in. One press runs the whole cycle: every group in turn (today one), each with its OWN progress bar — group name, a one-sentence caption of what it is doing, and a percentage — plus a Batal button and a "N diunduh, M diunggah" summary totalled across groups. One bar per group spans the WHOLE cycle: pull, merge, push and the closing pull are weighted into a single fraction that is clamped upward, so the bar never restarts or runs backwards at a phase boundary; only before the first page returns (no denominator yet) is it an indeterminate sliver. One bar per group is the point of the layout: a second group is another row, not another redesign. Sinkronisasi Ulang sets every group's bookmark to 0 and marks every synced row dirty (content and clocks untouched) before running the same flow — it never deletes a row.
sync_ui_design.background_task: The run is not the screen's: the service forks it as a background task and the screen only reads it. Leaving the screen keeps the run going, one run at a time, and only Batal stops it (cooperatively: the state reads "Membatalkan" until the in-flight transaction or upload chunk settles). Closing anything never cancels.
sync_ui_design.status_pill: A small floating pill at the bottom-left corner, on every authenticated screen (the shell's BottomRail, which the cart's SaveError banner also uses so the two cannot overlap). Green, `rounded-full`, with a pulsing dot while a run is in flight; red with an alert glyph when the last run failed, staying until its dialog is closed or the next run starts — a background failure has no other way of reaching the operator. No pill while nothing runs and the last run succeeded. Its text never changes during a run (no counters, no entity names), so the `aria-live` region announces "Menyinkronkan" once instead of narrating every frame. Clicking it opens a dialog: phase sentence, progress bar, elapsed seconds, current entity and frame count, the "N diunduh, M diunggah" summary or the error, Batal (only while running) and Tutup. Nothing starts a sync but the operator.

pages.description: Every page below is routed and runs on the services layer. The two Dev/ pages exist only in a DEV build. Page behaviour is described from the code, not from an older plan.

page.name: login
page.description: Two-mode login over the cashier service. With no cashiers it shows FreshForm (Buat Toko: shop name, owner name, password), otherwise LoginForm (pick a cashier, enter the password). Already-signed-in users are redirected by AuthLayout.
page.fresh_form: Buat Toko: name, password, confirm. Creates the first admin (Rust hash_password → cashier.add), signs the session in through auth.set, and lands on /setting so the shop identity can be filled in next. It does not write the shop name itself.
page.login_form: Lists cashier names, verifies with the Rust verify_password command, then auth.set.

page.name: home
page.description: Beranda: a workspace, not a launcher. Header (shop name, day), three zero-blocking stat cards (masuk, keluar, utang) that each gate only the value they need, the day's ledger (six rows, reserved height, newest first), and — admins only — the pocket card. The menu grid of destinations sits underneath. Data comes from one provider with one key per question (today, yesterday, records, debt, pockets), each driven by the record revision so a commit reaches the page while it is open. Role is part of the provider deps, and the pockets key is left unsubscribed for cashiers.

page.name: pos
page.description: The sale screen. Two panels: the top walks the goods then the charges (two stages), the bottom carries the split payment rows, the change and the grand total. The cart and the stage live in the URL (`?draft=`, `?stage=`); F1/F2/F12, Ctrl+←/→ and Ctrl+0..3 are the operator's path. Listing search also returns active combos; choosing one adds ordinary listing rows and transaction-wide Extra snapshots in one draft update. Nothing waits as a block: drafts, methods, customers and extras are registered on one page-data provider and start together. Bayar is the shared useSubmitCart flow (mode incoming): submit → transaction.add.draft, then the completion dialog with print and undo. See <cart>.

page.name: restock
page.description: The purchase screen — Pos's shape buying instead of selling. Three stages (goods, charges, payment) because a purchase settles through the stage panel; drafts, methods and suppliers load together. F2 opens the payment stage and puts the cursor on its first amount. A credit purchase is a settled flag on the same submit (useSubmitCart with credit), and the completion dialog prints the tender it took. Same shared cart machinery as Pos.

page.name: transaction
page.description: `/transaction` — an arbitrary record, typed by hand: no catalog, no search, no stages, no precision, no customer. Each tab is a real tx_records row flagged ADJUSTMENT_CART_FLAG; its lines are number extras, its direction, note and one payment live beside them. Committing calls record.add.adjustment (a records row flagged RECORD_FLAG_ADJUSTMENT, extras only, no stock) and deletes the tab. The tab is the source of truth: every edit goes through the service and the screen renders the stream.

page.name: product
page.description: The catalogue. One live list key feeds both the rows and the counts: search (fuzzy ladder, 250 ms debounce), kind/stock/margin/publish (Terbit, Belum terbit, Semua) filters, name/price/capital/stock sort with an "auto" relevance sort while searching, table or card view, and pagination — all in the URL (useListState) so a link reopens the same view; the view alone is also mirrored to the config service's `product-view` preference, so a bare `/products` reopens on the last layout. Admins get the floating add button. Rows gate on the key; the toolbar and footer are static.

subpages.subpage: The product form: info, one or more listings (code, price, unit, kind), alternative names, properties, images, initial stock lots.

Detail with three sub-tabs: Info (info/listings/properties/stock lots and the event journal), Image (gallery, drag-order, cover, delete), Performance (sales, margin and stock events over a range, lazy-loaded).

page.name: records
page.description: The day's history over the record service, read one local day at a time (useTime) and narrowed by a `query` matched in SQL. Two panes: the day's records on the left, the selected record on the right. Refetches keep the previous day on screen and fade it instead of blanking. Modes: Masuk (sale: money in, stock consumed) and Keluar (purchase: money out, stock received); the sort column/direction is in the URL (useOrder).

subpages.subpage: Comprehensive search across listing lines by name, mode and date range, with a capped page and the total match count.

One record in full, with Detail | Resi tabs in the URL. Detail shows the ledger (identity band, goods, charges, parties, totals, methods, images) and, admin only, the shelf actions: edit note, move the date, change mode, edit split payments, toggle credit, delete. The goods table shows each line's Modal on a purchase — and, for an admin, on a sale too, with a pencil that opens the escape hatch for a wrong recorded cost (`set.lineCapital`: warning, new figure, required reason, appended to the note). Resi is the receipt it prints (laid out and rendered by the Rust print_receipt command).

page.note: The record list does not filter RECORD_FLAG_ADJUSTMENT yet, so a dual charge's extras-only twin shows as a goods-less outcoming row — see <open_questions>.

page.name: money
page.description: Pockets ("kantong") over the money service. A draggable grid of cards (name, relative time, latest balance) — dragging persists the order through set.ordering — plus the Kantong Baru dialog. The page redirects non-admins itself because the alt+4 shortcut is not role-gated.

subpages.subpage: One pocket's ledger over a date range in the URL: editable name and type, the entries table (day, date, time, diff for `change` pockets, value, note), expandable rows, a settings dialog with delete-pocket / JSON upload / JSON download, and the new-entry button.

page.name: category
page.description: The category catalog, for admins: a list of names with inline rename and a delete dialog, plus a create dialog. The product form's picker reads the same list (its own page-data key), and `product.set.categories` writes the links. A name typed into that picker is created by the product's own save, not here, so the catalogue gains a row only where one was needed. Deleting a category keeps the products and leaves their links as orphans.

page.name: combo
page.description: Admin-only management for reusable combo templates: name, active state, ordered listing components with quantities, references to existing Extra presets, and an optional cover image. In POS search, active combos match their own name and component listing/product names; a selected combo expands into regular cart rows. Preset Extras retain transaction-wide behavior and are not linked to their component lines.

page.name: extra
page.description: The surcharge catalog: a fuzzy search box over a table of name, kind (Angka/Persen) and value, each row linking into its detail. Admins get a create button and the edit form (name, value, kind, and the dual flag); other roles see a read-only panel.

subpages.subpage: Create: name, kind, the amount in that kind's own field (dotted rupiah or clamped ±100 percent), and the dual flag.
Detail: edit form for admins (with delete), read-only info panel for users.

page.name: debt
page.description: Outstanding customer credit over record.get.debt(): every credit record, since paying one clears it. A summary card totals the rows with decimal arithmetic and a sortable table lists date, note, total and a link into the record; the sort is in the URL (useSort). Re-reads on the record revision, so settling or deleting a record updates it.

page.name: cashier
page.description: The cashier roster over the cashier service: name, role, add, rename, re-role and delete. A new account is created as a `user` with an empty password; the cashier sets their own from Setting → Profile. Static head and add button; the list is the only key.

page.name: customer

page.name: method
page.description: Payment methods over the method service. Tabs are the defaultable kinds (Transfer, Debit, QRIS) in the URL (useMethod); each tab lists the kind's named accounts plus its base method, with add, rename, set-as-default and soft delete. Static head and tabs; the catalog is the only key.

page.name: social
page.description: Receipt contact lines over the social service: name and value, add, edit, soft delete. Ordered by id so an edit never reshuffles the receipt.

page.name: analytics
page.description: A rail of five questions over one period. The period and bucket width live in the URL (useRange: presets 7/30/90 days, this month, this year; a hand-picked range clears the preset) and in the header, so switching pages never resets what you were looking at. The bodies are the lazy chart chunk; the rail and range bar are static. URLs are English; the visible labels stay Indonesian.

subpages.subpage: Arus Kas (Cashflow): money in vs out per bucket, with totals.

Laba (Profit): margin over the period — the stored cost where it is believable, and `min(10% of the line, Rp5.000)` per line where it is not (migration-54's repair plus an operator-set estimate, edited under the chart). The stat says how many lines were costed and how many were estimated.

Products: a totals band (total omzet, total laba, product count) then per-product qty/revenue/margin in a sortable, paginated table that expands to the individual lines, split by transaction kind. The totals are summed from the same rows as the table, so they follow the Masuk/Keluar switch; `total laba` counts only lines whose stored cost is believable (above zero, below the line's price) and its hint names how many lines are not, so a bad `modal` reads as a dash instead of a phantom loss. No chart, so no bucket width.
Time: sales per weekday and per hour, one week at a time.
Payments: what was tendered per method kind, plus the unpaid part of the period.

page.name: network
page.description: Jaringan (Product network): a co-occurrence graph of products, built on demand from the shared analytics scope. A Rust command aggregates pairs per record in seven-day windows, computes lift, lays the graph out deterministically, and publishes a compact .kgr snapshot under app-data (separate from data.db and store.json). The layout shell is Analytics' (rail, range bar, `today` preset; body overflow hidden), with a Buat ulang button, a staged progress bar, pan/zoom canvas, viewport culling, mode (Jual/Beli), count-vs-lift edges, per-node top-k and a product cap.

page.name: setting
page.description: One nav source (util-nav.ts) drives the index card grid and the sidebar, including which roles may open each destination; each screen's header quotes that row verbatim. Below the destinations sits the one control that is not a page: the Tampilan zoom slider (100 / 150 / 200%), written through the zoom service.

subpages.subpage: Signed-in account: rename (cashier.set.name + auth.set) and change password (Rust hash, then cashier.set.password).

Shop identity (owner, address, header, footer) through info, plus the show-cashier toggle; every field label and the save button are static and only the values pulse. The form patches the current info instead of overwriting it.

JSON export (Rust export_file) and import for products and records, with the skipped-row panel and a derived success/warning/error toast (describeUpload). Above them sits the whole-install backup (Rust backup_data): one .zip of data.db (VACUUM INTO snapshot), store.json and a manifest, written through a Save dialog.
Printer picker, paper width in mm (Lebar Struk) and a test print, over the printer service and the Rust printer commands. The width decides how the receipt PDF is laid out.

The server address (editable, seeded with SYNC_DEFAULT_BASE_URL) + SYNC_TOKEN with a Cek button that pings /v2/health inline, the pull cursor, and the Sinkronisasi / Sinkronisasi Ulang actions with per-phase progress, over the sync service.

page.description: The page-data playground: a demo page with fast/slow/flaky keys, the Gate variants, stale and refreshing states, and the monitor that shows each key's status. It is also the place the legacy Result-based Gate still appears, labelled as such.

page.description: The page-cache inspector: entries by tag+deps, their kind, age, hits, stale/error state, plus clear/invalidate controls and the stats.

utilities.module: Money arithmetic for carts and records: lineSubtotal, lineGrandTotal, lineDiscountTotal, discountsEatLine, recalcDiscounts (clamped, order-dependent stack), withDerivedDiscounts, linesSubtotal, recalcExtras, extrasTotal, purchaseTotal, transactionGrandTotal, paidTotal, roundMoney. Decimal throughout.

module.entry: App version, kept in step with package.json, Cargo.toml, tauri.conf.json and specification.xml.
["cash", "qris", "transfer", "debit"] — the order the Ctrl+0..3 keys follow.
Display names, key hints, key → kind, and the four built-in ids (1000 cash, 1003 qris, 1001 transfer, 1002 debit).
0b1 — the "books twice" bit of an extra's flag.
250 ms for search filters, 100 ms for cart writes.
The runtime time zone, used by every date-range bound and every date format.

cn (tailwind-merge with the app's text-size tokens declared), numerish/numeric/integer (Zod string-number schemas that actually reject), capitalize (total on padded/empty names), formatError.
NotFound, InvokeError, InvalidCredential, IOError/ArrayBufferError/JsonError, TooBigError, DuplicateError. RedirectError was removed with the redirect loaders.
The two Tauri bcrypt bridges plus Unauthenticated. The session lives in the auth service.

saveBackup(store, onProgress): serialise the loaded store.json, then ask Rust (backup_data) for a `.zip` of the database, the store and a manifest, relaying one monotonic progress bar (stage keyword + whole-cycle percent) off a Tauri Channel. Cancelling is null, a failure is an IOError with the cashier sentence.
saveJson(defaultName, value): serialise, then ask Rust (export_file) where to write. Cancelling is null, a failure is an IOError with the cashier sentence.
Product-image files under AppData/images: save (mkdir on first use), load → object URL, del. The key is the image_name, never the row id.

The Rust printer bridges: getPrinters and printReceipt (which sends the receipt's data — record, lines, shop identity, contacts — plus the roll layout, and returns the spooler's sentence). The PDF itself is built in src-tauri/src/receipt/.
Fire-and-forget logging through plugin-log; a missing plugin or a rejected write never breaks the caller.
generateId() — a ULID for every row the app creates.
EARLIEST_EPOCH/FURTHEST_EPOCH and parseRange: URL epoch bounds that are safe for Temporal and fall back per bound.
describeUpload + notifyUpload: the one success/warning/error sentence for the three import panels.
canRead/writeText/readText: the async clipboard first, an execCommand("copy") fallback for the webview, and an honest "cannot read" for the paste-key path.

normalize (casefold/accents/punctuation, compact), quality (the match ladder, code grading and matchPosition), index-cache (the signature-gated index, parseQuery, the shared createMatcher/rankHits scoring and tie-breaks, toHit), listings (the restock catalogue index), eval (the labelled fixture set, metrics and ranking ablations behind `bun run eval:search`).

The receipt pipeline, on the Rust side: text.rs turns a record into TextData rows (header, lines and discounts, totals/extras/rounding/pay/change, the species/pieces and split-payment summary, footer and contacts); render.rs wraps the rows against the embedded Roboto metrics and writes the one-page PDF with printpdf, its height grown row by row; format.rs is the Indonesian rupiah formatting and the local dd-MM-yyyy / H:mm date. Covered by cargo test.

feature.name: sync_rebuild
feature.description: Build a sync service over the current schema (soft `_deleted_at`, nested product/record payloads, per-entity unsync reads) and restore the Sinkronisasi screen and floating status pill designed in <sync_ui_design>. The server contract is in backend-docs/openapi.yaml.

feature.name: sync_background
feature.description: Move the sync run out of the Sinkronisasi screen: the service forks it as a daemon (single-flight), progress becomes one coalesced SyncState stream, and the merge is applied in bounded slices with both conflict decisions moved into SQL inside the transaction, so a write that lands mid-merge (a sale, an edit) is never lost. Adds the bottom-left status pill + dialog and hoists the cart's SaveError banner into the same rail.

feature.name: record_list_flag_filter
feature.description: Filter RECORD_FLAG_ADJUSTMENT out of the /records list (or show the twin differently). Noted as the open piece in FLAGS.md: a dual charge's extras-only twin currently shows as a goods-less outcoming row.

feature.name: analytics_server_side
feature.description: Analytics currently reads every record in the range and aggregates in SQL per question. If a shop's history outgrows that, the aggregates move behind materialised per-day tables.

feature.name: product_event_batching
feature.description: Superseded by the byte-stream protocol: events travel as their own frames in the fixed entity order, so there is no per-product id list to batch.

feature.name: sync_automatic
feature.description: Manual only today: one button on Setting → Sinkronisasi. `service.sync.run()` is already an Effect fiber with a progress stream and a cancel path, so this is policy, not plumbing. Triggers: debounced ~30 s after a record commit, once on app start after the cart is restored, on window focus / machine resume, and a ~15 min idle safety net; never while `transaction` holds an uncommitted cart (a merge refreshes product refs). Retry transport failures with exponential backoff (5 s → 10 m, jitter); never auto-retry 401/400 — a wrong token needs the operator. Single-flight via the existing `running` ref. Requires sync_status_pill so a background write is never invisible.

feature.name: sync_status_pill
feature.description: The run is only visible on the Sinkronisasi screen, which is acceptable while sync is manual and wrong once it is automatic. The design exists (<sync_ui_design>): a compact pill in the AuthLayout showing phase, last success and a retry affordance, subscribing to the same `service.sync.progress` stream. UI work plus a decision on where a failure that happened off-screen gets acknowledged.

feature.name: sync_blob_frames
feature.description: Image ROWS sync (a restored device knows which picture belongs to which product/record); the bytes under AppData/images/ do not, so it renders placeholders. Needs the reserved `blob` frame (contract §9), /v1/blob/:sha256 backed by R2, and an `image_sha` column on `images` / `record_images` so a row names content rather than a local filename. Upload after the referencing row, download lazily with a placeholder, dedupe by content hash, and a GC pass for the bytes of replaced images.

feature.name: sync_upload_resume
feature.description: A run starts a fresh upload session, so a crash mid-push re-sends everything (nothing is lost — frames are idempotent — but a first full push over a slow uplink pays twice). One field fixes it: GET /v1/upload/:id must expose the session's `prefix_sha`. The client already persists `sync.upload_chain`, so `openSession` could verify at + frames + prefix against its own record and continue instead of deleting the session.

feature.name: sync_token_keychain
feature.description: `sync.token` is plain text in store.json. Move it to the OS credential store through a small Rust command pair (Windows Credential Manager, Secret Service on Linux), keeping only the endpoint in store.json. `config.get` reports whether a token is stored; a missing token becomes a re-enter state that does not wipe the cursors.

feature.name: sync_stale_notice
feature.description: A `stale` ack silently rewrites the local row — correct per contract §5.2, invisible to the operator, and a real event when it is a renamed product or a re-priced listing. Keep the last N stale merges (entity, id, changed columns, both clocks) and surface them on the Sinkronisasi screen ("3 data diperbarui dari server") behind a disclosure. No protocol change: the winning row already arrives in the ack.

feature.name: sync_multi_device
feature.description: The protocol is written for the general case (LWW, server tiebreak, `sync_seq` cursor) and the pull cursor refuses to advance past a second writer's rows. Unproven rather than missing: `stocks` is derived locally from the journal (both devices should reach the same lots — wants a test), `record_pair_id` may name a twin that arrives later, and there is no stable device id. Needs an X-Device-Id header, a two-mirror test over test-backend.ts, and only then the sanctioned `sync_change` log if re-materialising pull snapshots gets heavy.

feature.name: sync_per_entity_sessions
feature.description: One upload session covers all fourteen entities, so an oversized entity blocks everything behind it. Contract §12 sanctions a session per entity: simpler failure isolation, at the cost of more sessions. Worth doing only after sync_upload_resume, which removes most of the re-send that a failed session costs today.

feature.name: sync_tombstone_gc
feature.description: Soft-deleted rows are never removed on either side, so both databases grow with every deletion. A `_deleted_at` older than ~90 days and already synced could be purged — but only under a protocol rule that also stops a late-joining device from resurrecting it, since the tombstone is the only thing preventing that.

feature.name: sync_diagnostics
feature.description: Errors reach the app log (Setting → Log) but there is no sync-specific view: no last-run summary, no per-entity counts, no record of a 409 replay_mismatch or a chain divergence. A panel reading the same progress/report values would turn "it didn't sync" into one line.

feature.name: sync_ranged_first_sync
feature.description: A shop with years of history must upload all of it before the mirror is complete, and a restored device must download all of it to answer a question about today. A first-sync window ("last 12 months, then catch up") needs server support in the pull, plus a decision about what a partial mirror means for reports.

feature.name: sync_mobile_client
feature.description: The protocol admits one (no user table, one token, LWW). It would want the image blobs, a smaller pull page, and a read-only stance that never pushes a `record` — a phone should not become a second author of the sales history without an explicit decision.
